# ORDERING EXPLANATION: Unit/component tests run first since they are
# the fastest and cheapest - any genuine bug they catch stops the
# pipeline immediately, before spending time provisioning a database
# for integration tests or launching a browser for E2E tests. Integration
# tests run next, since they're more expensive than unit tests but still
# cheaper than E2E tests. E2E tests run last specifically because they
# are the slowest and most expensive tier, and should only run once
# every faster, cheaper tier has already confirmed no obvious problems
# exist - exactly this lesson's fail-fast principle.
validationRules: Tests must run in the order: unit/component, then integration, then E2E - matching the fail-fast, cheapest-first principle
The integration test step must include a provisioned test database service, not a real production database
The deploy job must include a genuine dependency (needs: test or equivalent) on the test job's success
Must include a written explanation of the fail-fast reasoning behind this specific ordering
hints: The exact specific syntax matters less than correctly capturing the conceptual structure: cheapest/fastest tests first, most expensive/slowest tests last
The test database service should be a genuinely fresh, isolated instance, not a connection to any real, persistent database
Your explanation should explicitly reference saving time/resources by failing fast on cheap tests before running expensive ones

finalModuleProject.title: Build A Complete, Pyramid-Shaped Test Suite Wired Into A CI/CD Pipeline
finalModuleProject.goal: Synthesize everything from all 6 lessons — the testing pyramid, Jest unit tests, React Testing Library component tests, Supertest integration tests, Playwright E2E tests, and CI/CD pipeline configuration — by building one genuinely complete, correctly-proportioned test suite for a small full stack feature, wired into an automated, fail-fast pipeline.
finalModuleProject.description: Choose a small full stack feature you've built earlier in this curriculum (a contact form, a comment system, or similar) and build a complete, four-tier test suite for it: mocked unit tests for its core business logic, React Testing Library tests for its frontend component(s) including loading/error/success states, Supertest integration tests for its backend endpoint(s) with proper test database lifecycle management, and exactly one Playwright E2E test covering its single most critical complete user flow. Wire all four tiers into a CI/CD pipeline configuration with correct fail-fast ordering and a deployment job genuinely gated on test success. Conclude with a written explanation of why each specific test lives at its specific tier, referencing this module's pyramid reasoning directly.

requirements.requirement: At least 3 mocked unit tests covering the feature's core business logic, including both success and failure/edge cases
At least 2 React Testing Library tests for the feature's frontend component, including explicit verification of a loading state's presence and subsequent absence
At least 3 Supertest integration tests for the feature's backend endpoint(s), with correct beforeAll/afterEach/afterAll test database lifecycle management
Exactly one Playwright E2E test covering the feature's single most critical, complete user flow through a real browser
A complete CI/CD pipeline configuration running all four tiers in correct fail-fast order, with a deployment job genuinely dependent on test success
A written explanation justifying each test's specific tier placement, explicitly referencing this module's pyramid reasoning

rubric.criterion: Unit tests correctly mock all external dependencies and cover both success and failure cases
Component tests correctly verify observable behavior, including explicit loading-state absence verification
Integration tests correctly manage test database lifecycle and cover authentication/validation edge cases where applicable
The E2E test correctly covers a genuinely critical, complete user flow through a real browser
The CI/CD pipeline is correctly ordered (fail-fast) with deployment genuinely gated on test success
The written justification correctly and specifically applies the pyramid's reasoning to each test's actual tier placement

finalModuleProject.certificateUnlockCondition: Score 70 or above on the rubric and complete all 6 lesson coding challenges.
